alternate_mechanisms.title: Ordered following versus post-proof dispersal
alternate_mechanisms.mechanism: The proof arrives through ordered succession: messenger, recitation, sheets, and writings follow one another coherently. Division is the counter-process in which recipients cease following, leave prior companionship, and disperse after the sequence has become clear.

alternate_mechanisms.title: Pure medium, upright content, failed reception
alternate_mechanisms.mechanism: Clarity, purified sheets, and upright writings jointly protect the source and transmission mechanism. The later division can therefore be explored as recipient-side concealment, interpretive error, or refusal rather than impurity in the proof itself; misreading remains a possibility, not an asserted universal cause.

alternate_mechanisms.title: Hospitality converted into relational rupture
alternate_mechanisms.mechanism: A scripture community has the latent capacity to recognize, welcome, and trust a messenger from the same divine source. Rejection converts that possible hospitality into disavowal; recitation is followed by abandonment, separation, and opposition.

alternate_mechanisms.title: Gift-transfer becomes entrusted liability
alternate_mechanisms.mechanism: Scripture was previously given, and the clear proof is now brought and presented. These transfers establish entrustment: what is received becomes a right or obligation that follows its holder. The same writing can release recipients from rejection while binding them to an accountable response.

alternate_mechanisms.title: Proof as non-coercive compulsion to decide
alternate_mechanisms.mechanism: The proof does not force assent, yet its manifest arrival makes neutrality harder to sustain. As discriminating testimony it compels judgment, exposes contest, and separates responses; the compulsion is evidentiary and responsible rather than coercive belief.
